source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Correct. Sensors and power-management circuitry stay on the other boards; the main board contains:

\- ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module
\- INA219 current monitor measuring the 3.3V rail
\- USB-C programming connector plus an LDO for standalone operation
\- All JST connectors for the power board, sensor board, display, PIR, touch inputs, LEDs, buttons, and reset
\- Supporting components including decoupling capacitors, pull-ups, series resistors, Schottky diodes, and a BOOT button

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: A reset button and a switch are included as well, and I think there are 2 additional buttons.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Here is the complete mapping:

\- The J\_BTN3 panel button is assigned to GPIO6
\- The J\_BTN4 panel button is assigned to GPIO7
\- The J\_SW panel slide switch is assigned to GPIO8
\- The J\_RESET panel reset button connects EN to GND
\- The J\_TOUCH capacitive-touch connector uses TTP223 and is assigned to GPIO11
\- The J\_TOUCH2 capacitive-touch connector uses TTP223 and is assigned to GPIO14
\- The BOOT button is on-board only for development and is not panel-mounted
